newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close lower but mood positive.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close lower but mood positive.

text.p: Argentine stocks snapped a seven-session rise and closed moderately lower Wednesday, anticipating a round of profit-taking on Wall Street after a rally which capped the U.S. presidential vote, dealers said.

"This correction may continue for the next few sessions, chiefly because there is very little volume," said broker Dario Lizzano at Santander bank. "But the market should resume its rise by the middle of next week when private pension fund cash flows start to pick up."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 0.7 percent to 579.73, while the broad market eased 0.5 percent.
The MerVal had gained 4.3 percent in the previous seven sessions.
"I see more upside now in stocks quoted strictly locally, like the steel and petrochemical companies. But the heavyweight stocks listed abroad should stay fairly rangebound," said Lizzano.
Despite the precautionary pullback on the bolsa, analysts welcomed the outcome of the U.S. elections which they said spells continued stability in the international markets.
"There were no nasty surprises and it's just as we expected," said Augusto Marinozzi of Mildesa traders.
Floor volume totaled 17.6 millon pesos against 18.8 million Tuesday, while over-the-counter deals slowed to 69.3 million pesos from 76.9 million Tuesday.
Losers beat winners 26 to 14 and 20 issues closed flat.
The only blue-chip gainers were petrochemical concern Ipako, which jumped 2.3 percent, and Banco Frances and Banco de Galicia, up 1.5 percent and 0.4 percent, respectively.
Heaviest losses were in oil firm Sol Petroleo, agricultural holding company Cresud and construction stock Polledo, off 5.2 percent, 3.4 percent and 3.0 percent, respectively.

Market bellwether YPF lost 1.1 percent in the session although its third quarter results came in above expectations early in the day. The oil giant was raised to buy from long-term buy by Robert Fleming late Wednesday.
"YPF just followed the general market trend. But its medium-term outlook is strong," said Lizzano.
